newsitem.title: FINLAND: Clinton, Yeltsin hit upbeat note at summit dinner.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Yeltsin hit upbeat note at summit dinner.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin struck a positive and jovial note at their first summit session on Thursday, spokesmen for the two leaders said.

Briefing reporters after the two leaders dined with Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari, White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters: "The president and Yeltsin were clearly striking a tone for the meeting which seemed to be very positive. There was a lot of banter back and forth."

Russian presidential spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky, at a separate briefing, said: "You can say that the two presidents immediately renewed their friendly contacts. There were a lot of jokes...and of course...it did not pass without jokes about the health of both the presidents."
Clinton is temporarily confined to a wheelchair following surgery for a leg injury and Yeltsin has only recently emerged from months of illness following a heart operation.
McCurry said the two men had not attempted to get into serious negotiations on NATO expansion plans or other subjects over the dinner, but would do so at the main talks on Friday.
He quoted Clinton as saying of Yeltsin: "I think he really came here to do business."
Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin had told him he felt the two presidents would be able to tackle their tricky summit agenda when they got down to talks.
He quoted Yeltsin as saying: "I think that judging by the mood of both presidents we showed complete determination to tackle the problems worrying us and get results on the most difficult questions."

Yastrzhembsky added, "The president of Russia...has felt a certain mood, and the American president must also have sensed that the president (Yeltsin) came here with the intention of getting down to concrete business and leaving behind the burden of the problems which are worrying us all now."
